summary.value: The Romagnola is an old farmyard chicken from Emilia-Romagna in Italy, once common around Ravenna, Forli-Cesena and Bologna. In the mid 1900s breeders at Rovigo and Ravenna fixed two color types, a silver and a golden, both flecked with black, though the breed still varies a lot in color. Skin is mostly creamy white, the legs run from yellow to almost black, the earlobes are cream with a hint of blue and the comb is single. It is a light, fine-boned bird: roosters weigh about 4.4 to 5.5 pounds and hens a little over 4. Hens lay around 150 white eggs a year, each fairly large at about 60 grams. It is kept for both eggs and meat, and the young grow fast and have good flavor. The breed nearly vanished before a recovery project led from Parma began, and numbers are still very small.
